messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams Mobile: Introducing shared call history in the Queues app
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams mobile Queues app now offers shared call history for authorized representatives, showing missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. Rolling out worldwide in December 2026, it helps teams manage calls efficiently with status updates and filtering, extending desktop features to mobile without new admin actions.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and why

We are introducing shared call history in the Queues app on Microsoft Teams mobile, allowing authorized call queue representatives to view calls handled across their queue. This includes missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. By extending the existing desktop experience to mobile, we are helping teams coordinate customer follow-ups, avoid duplicate callbacks, and manage calls more efficiently while working away from their desks.

Rollout schedule

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout will begin in early December 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-December 2026.

Impact on your organization

Who is affected

  • Representatives and supervisors with access to shared call history in the Queues app, which is included with a Teams Premium license.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams mobile, Queues app

What will happen

  • Authorized representatives can view shared call history across their call queue, including missed, answered, outgoing, and voicemail calls. Shared call history on mobile uses the same administrative settings as the desktop experience.

  • Users can filter call history by resolution status to identify calls that need attention.

  • Users can tap a call to view details, including the caller, call type, time, voicemail or forwarding information, and a timeline of the call's progression through the queue.

  • The system automatically marks missed calls as Unresolved, allowing representatives to identify customers who need follow-up.
  • Users can change missed call statuses to In progress or Resolved. All queue members with access to shared call history can see the updated status, who made the change, and when.
  • Users without shared call history enabled will continue to see only their personal call history.

Action required and recommendations

No new administrative action is required for this rollout. We recommend that you inform call queue representatives about the new mobile experience, particularly how to update missed call statuses to avoid duplicate follow-ups.

  • If your organization already uses shared call history, eligible users will automatically receive the mobile experience.
  • If shared call history is not enabled, you can enable it in the Teams admin center by creating a Shared Call History template and assigning it to your call queues. You can grant access to all queue members or restrict access to authorized users.

Learn more

  • Planning - Shared Call History for voice applications - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

Compliance considerations

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: Audio announcement for Recording and Transcription
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams now supports an optional audio announcement when recording or transcription starts, configurable via Meeting and Calling Policies. Rolling out from May 2026 to January 2027 worldwide. No admin action required; default is off. Compliance recording is not supported with this feature.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

The recording feature in Microsoft Teams now supports an audio announcement for Teams meetings and calls. With this new functionality, admins can enable a policy that plays an audio announcement when recording or transcription starts. This can be applied tenant-wide or to specific groups. The announcement helps ensure allowed participants who are permitted by policy are informed and improves accessibility awareness. This setting is available in both Meeting Policy and Calling Policy.

Rollout Schedule:

Public Preview (Worldwide): We began rolling out on early May 2026 and expect to complete by mid-December 2026.

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

General Availability (GCC): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

General Availability (GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out on mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by late January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

None.

Action Required/Recommendations:

No admin action is required. The default audio announcement policy is OFF; it can be turned on as needed.

Compliance considerations:

Confirmed that compliance recording is not supported with this feature. Review as appropriate for your organization.

messageCenterItems.title: Microsoft Teams: End of support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17
messageCenterItems.summary: Microsoft Teams will end support for iOS 17 and iPadOS 17 starting mid-December 2026, requiring iOS/iPadOS 18 or later for new releases. Existing versions will keep working without support. Organizations should notify users, encourage OS upgrades, update policies, and revise support documentation accordingly.
messageCenterItems.body:
What and Why:

Microsoft Teams is ending support for upcoming builds on iOS 17 and iPadOS 17. As this change rolls out, new Teams releases will require iOS 18 or later on iPhone and iPadOS 18 or later on iPad.

Rollout Schedule:

General Availability (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in mid-December 2026 and expect to complete by early January 2027.

Impact on Your Organization:

Users whose devices remain on iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 will not be able to install newer Teams releases that require a newer operating system.

Teams versions already installed on these devices will continue functioning without official support. This change does not introduce a block on opening or signing in to those existing installations.

Action Required/Recommendations:

  • Identify devices running iOS 17 or iPadOS 17 and notify affected users.
  • Advise users to upgrade to a supported operating system, then update Teams through the Apple App Store, to continue receiving supported Teams releases.
  • Review any mobile device management (MDM) or app deployment policies that pin or require specific iOS/iPadOS versions, and update them to allow iOS 18/iPadOS 18 so affected devices are not blocked from upgrading.
  • Update internal support documentation and helpdesk guidance.

Learn more: Hardware requirements for Microsoft Teams.

Compliance considerations:

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.
